messages.subject: calculating effect size by script
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

 

I was trying to implement the measure of effect size for lmers as proposed
by Brysbaert and Stevens (2018), following Westfall et al. (2014):

Brysbaert, M. and Stevens, M. (2018). Power Analysis and Effect Size in
Mixed Effects Models: A Tutorial. Journal of Cognition, 1: 9, 1-20, DOI:
https://doi.org/10.5334/joc.10
<https://www.journalofcognition.org/articles/10.5334/joc.10/> .

 

It is basically dividing the mean difference by the square root of the sum
of all random-effect variances.

 

This is easy enough to do, but I was hoping to make things more efficient by
extracting at least the variances from the model output.

However, I have looked for quite some time at str(model.lmer) and
str(summary(model.lmer)) and have in vain searched for the variances of the
random effects.

 

(just in case it is unclear, I mean this ones):

Random effects:

Groups   Name        Variance Std.Dev.

item     boundaryC     2576    50.75  

 item.1   (Intercept)  14376   119.90  

 pp       segmentC      4403    66.36  

 pp.1     (Intercept)  77856   279.03  

 Residual             143852   379.28  

Number of obs: 1914, groups:  item, 96; pp, 42

 

Kind regards,

Holger

messages.subject: Re: calculating effect size by script
messages.body_plain:
Holger,

The VarCorr() function returns a list containing the variance-covariance
matrix for each random factor.

You can get the variances by applying the diag() function to each
element of that list.

Best,
-Dale

messages.body_plain:
Just it off curiosity (not having read the paper): Isn't that a
misleading/anti-conservative estimate of an effect size in that it ignores
uncertainty into the variance estimates?
